terms.job: want (a thing or to do something)
terms.trap: None big; the love meaning surprises learners
terms.why_fields: discussion: 'te quiero' is the other everyday job learners hear

terms.trap: using tú with strangers (covered on usted)
terms.why_fields: discussion: vos regions, so learners aren't thrown
anti_example: age with tener is the classic English-speaker slip

terms.trap: pairing usted with the tú verb form ('usted eres')
terms.why_fields: anti_example: the verb-form mismatch is what learners actually produce

terms.trap: English 'can' for learned skills → 'puedo nadar' instead of 'sé nadar'
terms.why_fields: anti_example: poder vs saber for skills

terms.job: 'you' for a group, any register (Latin America)
terms.why_fields: discussion: regional default, vosotros not needed
discussion: a + el → al, the common slip

terms.trap: avoiding the double negative: 'no quiero algo'
dropping que or using a: 'tengo a trabajar'
terms.why_fields: anti_example: learners calque 'have to' without que
